question.text: Under the ETD-specific rules described in the workbook, when is a tax audit mandatory for a derivative trader?

answer.text: Up to Rs. 2 crore turnover, audit applies only if profit/loss is below 6%, the trader has opted out of 44AD in any of the immediately five preceding years, and total income exceeds the basic exemption limit; Rs. 2-10 crore digital ETD has no audit; above Rs. 10 crore audit applies
Tax audit is always mandatory for derivative traders regardless of turnover
Only when losses exceed Rs. 50 lakh in a financial year
Tax audit applies only to equity derivatives, not to currency or interest rate derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook's ETD-specific guidance: up to Rs. 2 crore, audit only if profit/loss is below 6% AND the trader has opted out of 44AD in any one of the five immediately preceding years AND total income exceeds the basic exemption limit. Between Rs. 2 crore and Rs. 10 crore, ETD transactions are treated as more than 95% digital, so no audit is required. Above Rs. 10 crore, audit is required. The Trap: A blanket Rs. 1 crore Section 44AB threshold ignores the ETD-specific digital-transaction treatment that lifts the no-audit ceiling to Rs. 10 crore for ETD. Note: The Rs. 10 crore digital-transaction threshold and the sub-Rs. 2 crore 44AD-linked test are the practical drivers of ETD audit applicability.
